spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates why Appendix A's computed-value independence matters: a style tool's save (getComputedStyle readback) is lossless only when computed lists ignore the image count; the lossy path is the real engine behaviour, not a simulation.

interactive.rationale: Three position sliders, a visible-layer segment, and real Save/Restore actions that round-trip live computed style; the scene repaints from the restored string.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the hide→save→show→restore data-loss story; the page delivers it with the dots visibly piling up on lossy engines.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers lossy and lossless tiers, disables Restore until a save exists, and documents the authoring-time workaround (save the specified value) so the page is useful today.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus and Appendix A alongside sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's truncation/repetition and none-layer assertions are the exact mechanics behind the editor's save step.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless via CDP: full lossy sequence executed — slider moved, layers hidden, save captured 1 entry with an explicit damage warning, restore with 3 layers piled all dots at 20px 30px (screenshot shows the single visible dot and the ×3 computed list) — exactly the real bug; console clean; both viewports screenshot-verified.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts save-entry counts match the engine tier and the round-trip verdict (lossless on independent engines, honest lossy label otherwise).

design_system.rationale: All chrome from design-system variables; dots use accent variables with no text; pressed segment buttons invert with outline.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled sliders in a legend-titled fieldset, native buttons at 44px (Restore properly disabled until a save exists), scene has role=img tied to the readout, single polite readout.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3; editor panels stack, sliders span full width; both classes screenshot-verified.

openQuestions.title: Verify the lossless round-trip on real Chrome 158+/Canary
openQuestions.detail: On 158 the save with hidden layers must capture all 3 entries and the restore must put every dot back (editor-roundtrip-verdict assert true on the independent branch). Only the lossy branch could execute on this container's Chromium 141.

openQuestions.title: Inspect the accessibility tree with chrome-devtools-mcp
openQuestions.detail: Slider names, the disabled-state exposure of Restore, and the scene description were not inspected in the accessibility tree; chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable (project rule 7b).

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive two-panel editor layout stacking on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use auto-fit minmax grids so editor panels stack on narrow viewports with full-width controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The editor grid uses repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr)); sliders are display:block inline-size:100%.

guidanceConsulted.query: disabled action buttons and state exposure in a mini editor
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use the native disabled attribute for actions that are not yet valid rather than hiding them.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Restore is a native disabled button until the first save; it is never hidden, and the readout narrates every state change.

guidanceConsulted.query: touch target sizing for editor controls
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep controls at ≈44px minimum touch size.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Segments and action buttons declare min-height 44px; sliders get min-height 44px via their block layout.

summary: Product-case editor fully verified on Chromium 141 headless: the real lossy round-trip executed end-to-end (save captured one entry, restore visibly piled three dots onto it) with honest narration at each step; console clean; both viewports pass. The lossless 158 branch is pinned by the same code path and the conformance suite, pending a real 158 run.
